title: Help with collision on parallax map.

posts.author: colorofsand
posts.body:
Is there anyway to have a collision based on an image transparency and not a strict square? I heard about Rosedale and I don't feel comfortable spending 30 dollars on a single plug-in that might not work for me. But even still that doesnt really help me.
Basically I end up in situations where the player stops a good bit before (all sides) of an object and it looks silly. But adjusting the proportion would make it look stupid.
It would be great if I could just use map layer as a collision layer. I used galvs for layers if thats any help.
For the life of me I cant find a single tutorial that approaches this problem, they all go to region based Collison, but those regions are still just squares.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you would need a pixel based collision plugin for that.
I know that there were one or two of those for MV, but I don't know if they would be compatible to MZ.
In all cases, pixel based collisions require a lot more resources from the computer, so it will slow down most computers.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Rosedale gives you an external tool to import your project then draw custom polygon collisions for every tile on the tilesheet.
Technically you can get a similar effect with Altimit (free) with custom polygon collisions for events (not tiles) but there's no wysiwyg tool to draw them, you have to give it the numerical offsets.
Rosedale = custom tile collisions, but not event collisions.
Altimit = custom event collisions but not tile collisions.
I'll just say custom collisions are frankly a lot easier to do in other engines after working extensively with them in RPG Maker and then picking up another engine. I can literally just paint whatever collision map I want on its own layer in another engine and it's natively built in to the engine.
Tyruswoo Altimit Movement MZ | Tyruswoo Studio
Plugin for RPG Maker MZ. Add pixel movement to your game! Includes a command to recalculate tile boundaries, for compatibility with Tile Control MZ!

If you used Rosedale you would have to make the boundaries a series of polygonal tiles to recreate that. Same with Altimit but a series of polygonal events instead.
If you want to use the Q Plugins but it breaks follower movement you could use TyrusWoo Follower Control to overwrite default follower behavior and make it whatever you want.
